---
title: "Teams & scoreboard"
---

The ESPN cross-league surface is **uniform**: the same loader name shape works
for every league. This guide shows the teams directory and a past-dated
scoreboard, each rendered as a real frame at build time.

## Teams — the uniform `espn_<sport>_teams()` shape

```{python}
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams
from sportsdataverse.nfl import espn_nfl_teams
from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_teams
from sportsdataverse.nhl import espn_nhl_teams

nba = espn_nba_teams()
print("NBA teams frame:", nba.shape)
nba.columns
```

Every league returns the same tidy column set. Selecting the three columns most
readers care about, across four leagues:

```{python}
import polars as pl

frames = {
    "NBA": espn_nba_teams(),
    "NFL": espn_nfl_teams(),
    "MLB": espn_mlb_teams(),
    "NHL": espn_nhl_teams(),
}

summary = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "league": list(frames.keys()),
        "n_teams": [f.height for f in frames.values()],
        "example_team": [
            f.select("team_display_name").row(0)[0] for f in frames.values()
        ],
    }
)
summary
```

A closer look at the MLB directory — the first ten teams:

```{python}
espn_mlb_teams().select(
    ["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_location", "team_name"]
).head(10)
```

## Scoreboard — a stable past-dated call

Scoreboards take a `dates` argument (`YYYYMMDD`). Using a **past** date keeps the
example reproducible — the slate is final and won't change between renders.

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_scoreboard

sb = espn_mlb_scoreboard(dates="20240615")   # a settled 2024 regular-season date
print("scoreboard frame:", sb.shape)
sb.columns[:18]
```

A few human-readable columns from that slate:

```{python}
keep = [c for c in ["id", "name", "short_name", "status_type_detail"] if c in sb.columns]
sb.select(keep).head(8)
```

::: {.callout-note}
Because `execute: freeze: auto` is set project-wide, re-rendering this page does
**not** re-hit ESPN unless the `.qmd` source changes — the executed output is
cached in `_freeze/`. That also turns the examples into a lightweight
integration test: if a loader's output shape drifts, the re-render fails.
:::
